agenda: The situation concerning the Democratic Republic of the Congo
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: France’s objectives are to secure an immediate halt to the M23/RDF offensive, affirm DRC sovereignty and humanitarian access, and anchor the response in MONUSCO’s mandate and the Luanda/Nairobi processes. The most difficult points will be explicitly naming and demanding the withdrawal of Rwandan Defence Forces, language on sanctions readiness, and balancing those demands with FDLR/DRC obligations so the text can attract at least nine votes without a veto.

Insert 'in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and based on credible and verifiable evidence' after 'including targeted sanctions' and before 'against individuals and entities'.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft's core objectives, including the demand for M23's withdrawal, cessation of external support, respect for DRC sovereignty, and unimpeded humanitarian access. We request that OP11 explicitly refer to the African Union Peace and Security Council, and that OP14's readiness to consider targeted sanctions be qualified as being in accordance with the Charter and based on credible and verifiable evidence. These amendments would strengthen the text's legitimacy and its alignment with African-led processes.
messages.China: China supports the overall objective of de-escalating the situation in eastern DRC and upholds the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region. We have serious concerns about the explicit attribution to the Rwandan Defence Forces and the open-ended sanctions language, which risk complicating African-led mediation efforts. We propose replacing specific references to Rwanda with generic language on all external parties, and narrowing OP14 to existing sanctions procedures, solid evidence and support for political dialogue. If these changes are reflected, China would be prepared to support the draft; otherwise we would have to abstain.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft’s clear condemnation of M23, Rwandan military support and the demands for withdrawal, humanitarian access and accountability. We ask that OP14 be strengthened from readiness to consider sanctions to readiness to adopt targeted sanctions, with the 1533 Committee tasked to prioritize designations. We also ask for explicit WPS language in OP11 and ICC cooperation in OP10, consistent with Denmark’s long-standing positions.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft's firm condemnation of M23 and of all external support, including by Rwandan Defence Forces, and the demand for immediate withdrawal. We would like the text to reflect the risk of a wider regional war and to anchor humanitarian access in the humanitarian principles, including across conflict lines and borders. We also ask the penholder to include language on women's full and meaningful participation in the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft’s core demands and the clear condemnation of M23 and external support. We seek refinements to reinforce African-led Luanda and Nairobi processes, ensure humanitarian access reaches Goma, Bukavu and conflict-affected populations across lines, and anchor any sanctions in the UN sanctions regime and credible information.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft’s core objectives, including condemnation of M23, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC, and the demands for cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of external forces. We ask the penholder to strengthen language on tracking financial flows linked to illegal natural-resource exploitation, consistent with Pakistan’s long-standing position, and to safeguard MONUSCO’s capacity to implement its mandate. We also seek criteria-based and consultative language on any additional measures, in close coordination with the African Union and regional mechanisms.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft’s core objectives and would vote in favour with these refinements. We ask the penholder to anchor the text explicitly in Article 2(4) of the Charter, strengthen OP6 on safe passage and non-refoulement, and strengthen OP14 from readiness to intention to consider targeted sanctions. Panama remains firmly committed to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region and to the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft as a strong and balanced response to the deteriorating situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. We welcome its clear demands for cessation of hostilities, withdrawal of M23 and Rwandan Defence Forces, protection of civilians, unimpeded humanitarian access, and the safety of MONUSCO and humanitarian personnel. We encourage the Council to remain united behind the text and to continue supporting regional mediation through the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
messages.Russian Federation: We thank France for the draft and share the Council’s concern at the grave situation in eastern DRC. Russia can support a balanced text that demands cessation of hostilities and respect for DRC sovereignty, but it must avoid prejudging attribution and must not create an automatic sanctions track. We ask the penholder to reflect our changes to PP3, OP2 and OP8 and, above all, to remove the reference to targeted sanctions in OP14; with those adjustments we can support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks France and supports the thrust of the draft. We ask that OP11 explicitly anchor MONUSCO's continued support for the Luanda process and the reinforced ad hoc verification mechanism, consistent with our prior co-penholder statement. We also seek a conditions-based safeguard on any further adjustments to MONUSCO's deployment so that current crisis conditions do not create a security vacuum or weaken protection of civilians.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for a strong draft and supports its core demands, especially the condemnation of support to M23 and the demand for Rwandan withdrawal. We would like OP2 to match OP1’s immediacy and unconditionality, and we ask that OP14 explicitly list conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children as sanctions criteria. We also encourage a reference to the International Criminal Court in OP10, as applicable, to strengthen accountability.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as a balanced and necessary response to the escalating crisis in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It upholds the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region, condemns support to armed groups, and anchors the response in African-led processes including Luanda, Nairobi, the African Union, EAC and SADC. We urge swift adoption and full compliance by all parties.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the thrust of the draft and its clear message to M23 and the Rwandan Defence Forces. We ask the penholders to reflect our long-standing insistence that MONUSCO’s support to SAMIDRC must not draw MONUSCO into combat or affect its ability to deliver its mandate. We also seek stronger humanitarian access language and reporting on MONUSCO’s impartiality and the impact of support to SAMIDRC.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the draft’s clear condemnation of M23 and its explicit naming of Rwandan Defence Forces support, and we can support the text with targeted refinements. We ask that OP8 explicitly exclude MONUSCO involvement in combat operations, consistent with resolution 2746, and that OP14 make clear that direct or indirect support to M23, including by RDF personnel, is a sanctions trigger. We also suggest OP15 require reporting on Rwanda’s compliance with OP2.

replies.Algeria: partially accepted: AU Peace and Security Council added; OP16 includes Charter and evidence safeguards without restoring targeted-sanctions language.
replies.China: partially accepted: OP16 narrowed sanctions and added Charter safeguards; explicit RDF references retained.
replies.Denmark: partially accepted: ICC and 1533 Committee references added; targeted-sanctions readiness not included.
replies.Greece: accepted: regional-war risk, humanitarian principles and WPS language included.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: OP7 and OP13 reflect requested geography/process language; OP16 lacks explicit targeted-sanctions regime wording.
replies.Pakistan: accepted: financial-flows OP added, MONUSCO capacity safeguard and AU consultation included.
replies.Panama: partially accepted: Article 2(4) and non-refoulement included; OP16 not strengthened to intention/adopt.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: OP16 removes targeted-sanctions language and adds due-process safeguards; explicit RDF references and 30-day reporting retained.
replies.Sierra Leone: accepted: MONUSCO support/verification and conditions-based deployment safeguard included.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: OP2 immediacy, ICC reference, and CRSV/children criteria included.
replies.United Kingdom: accepted: combat exclusion, strategic priorities, humanitarian access and reporting requests included.
replies.United States: partially accepted: OP9 combat exclusion and OP17 reporting included; RDF support appears in OP16 for Committee consideration, not as explicit sanctions trigger.

steps.summary: The revision preserves the strong demands on M23/RDF withdrawal and humanitarian access while removing the explicit targeted-sanctions formulation to address Russia’s red line and adding many cross-regional safeguards. It should retain broad support, with China and Russia likely abstaining rather than blocking.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the inclusion of the AU Peace and Security Council in OP13 and the Charter, credible-evidence and non-interference safeguards in OP16, which address our earlier concerns. The text upholds DRC sovereignty and territorial integrity, supports African-led processes and humanitarian access, and maintains a balanced approach to accountability and regional dialogue. Algeria is therefore prepared to support the draft as it stands.
messages.China: China supports Council unity and a political settlement through the Luanda and Nairobi processes. The revised OP16 safeguards are welcome, but China continues to have difficulty with the Council singling out the Rwandan Defence Forces in PP3, OP2 and OP16; we ask the penholder to use neutral language on external military support and presence while retaining the demand that all unauthorized foreign forces respect the DRC's sovereignty and withdraw. With these adjustments China can support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes the revised text and the inclusion of the ICC and 1533 Committee references, and strongly supports the draft’s demands on M23/RDF withdrawal, humanitarian access and MONUSCO. We continue to believe the Council should signal readiness to use targeted sanctions against those responsible, including through the 1533 Committee, and ask the penholder to add that language to OP16. We can support the text if this is reflected.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised text as circulated. Our previous concerns on regional escalation risk, humanitarian principles and access, and women’s participation have been addressed, and the draft maintains a clear focus on sovereignty, protection of civilians, MONUSCO’s safety and accountability. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of the requested humanitarian geography and Luanda/Nairobi process language. We still ask that OP16 explicitly anchor any consideration of additional measures in the existing 1533 sanctions regime and in credible, verifiable information. This would strengthen consistency with Council practice and the A3+ call for evidence-based, regionally consulted action without prejudging specific designations.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for incorporating key concerns in the revised text, including the financial-flows paragraph, the MONUSCO capacity safeguard, and the AU consultation language. We support the current draft and encourage all parties to respect sovereignty and territorial integrity and to engage in good faith through the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Pakistan remains committed to MONUSCO's mandate and the safety of peacekeepers.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the revised draft and appreciates the inclusion of Article 2(4) and non-refoulement. To make the Council's response credible, OP16 should express an intention to adopt targeted sanctions, not merely reaffirm conditions for considering measures. Panama will not block the text but asks the penholder to strengthen this paragraph before the vote.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised draft as a balanced and timely response to the escalation in eastern DRC. We welcome the clear demands for cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of external military support, as well as the emphasis on humanitarian access, protection of civilians and the safety of MONUSCO personnel. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and proceed to a vote without further amendment.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports Council unity on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the need to protect civilians, but we cannot accept unverified attribution and selective naming of Rwanda in a Chapter VII text. We ask the penholder to restore balanced language on external support pending verification, replace demands on Rwandan forces with calls upon Rwanda, and remove Rwanda-specific reporting in OP17. We are ready to support a balanced text that reinforces the Luanda and Nairobi processes and avoids sanctions-driven approaches.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current text as revised. We welcome the inclusion of the conditions-based deployment safeguard for MONUSCO and the explicit support for the Luanda process and the reinforced ad hoc verification mechanism. These elements reflect our priorities on protecting civilians, preserving MONUSCO’s mandate, and advancing African-led mediation. We call on all Council members to unite behind this resolution and will vote in favour.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholders for incorporating its proposals on the immediacy of Rwandan withdrawal, the ICC reference in accountability, and conflict-related sexual violence and grave violations against children in the sanctions-related paragraph. We support the current text as a balanced and necessary response to the escalation in eastern DRC. We urge all Council members to unite and adopt it without delay, and stress that its implementation, including protection of civilians, humanitarian access and accountability, must be the priority.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the current text as drafted. It reflects our priorities on sovereignty, non-interference, civilian protection, humanitarian access and African-led regional processes, while demanding an end to external support for M23 and the withdrawal of Rwandan forces. We have no amendments at this stage and would vote in favour.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the revised text. We welcome that our earlier requests on MONUSCO’s support to SAMIDRC, humanitarian access across front lines, and reporting on impartiality and non-involvement in combat operations have been incorporated. We have no further changes and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft. It reflects our priority of naming Rwandan Defence Forces support to M23, demanding the immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal, and requiring reporting on Rwanda’s compliance. We appreciate the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier requests, including the explicit exclusion of MONUSCO from combat operations and Group of Experts reporting on RDF support, and we call for the Council to adopt the text promptly.

replies.China: accepted: neutralized external support language while retaining withdrawal and reporting demands.
replies.Denmark: partially accepted: OP16 expresses readiness to consider targeted measures, without mandatory prioritization.
replies.Guyana: accepted: OP16 anchors additional measures in the 1533 regime and credible information.
replies.Panama: partially accepted: OP16 signals readiness to consider targeted measures but not an intention to adopt.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: removed Rwanda-specific attribution and adjusted OP17, but retained withdrawal demands and sanctions readiness.
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: retained strong withdrawal and reporting provisions but neutralized RDF attribution for P5 unity.

steps.summary: The revision bridges P5 concerns by replacing Rwanda-specific attribution with neutral external-actor language while preserving M23 withdrawal, foreign-force withdrawal, humanitarian access, MONUSCO, and accountability. It partially accommodates sanctions calls through a 1533-based readiness clause and extends reporting to 60 days. The text should secure at least nine votes, with possible abstentions from Russia and the United States.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria’s position supports the draft’s emphasis on DRC sovereignty, cessation of hostilities, withdrawal of M23 and foreign forces, humanitarian access, and African-led political processes. It therefore votes in favour while underscoring due process and AU consultation on sanctions.
reasons.China: China’s requested changes neutralized language on external support, aligning the text with its support for DRC sovereignty, ceasefire, regional dialogue and African-led processes; it therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the draft’s demands for M23 withdrawal, an end to external support, humanitarian access and accountability, and its partial acceptance of Denmark’s sanctions language is sufficient to vote in favour while noting a remaining concern.
reasons.France: France is the draft’s penholder and has consistently condemned M23 and external military support to it while backing DRC sovereignty, humanitarian access, MONUSCO and the Luanda process. Voting yes advances France’s stated policy and preserves Council unity on the crisis.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports UN Security Council action upholding sovereignty, territorial integrity and international law in the DRC, and as an EU member aligns with France and partners on condemning M23 advances and external military support while backing regional political processes and MONUSCO. The draft also contains no unacceptable elements requiring abstention or veto.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana had signalled support with changes and its requested OP16 language was accepted, aligning the text with its emphasis on credible sanctions follow-up. It will vote yes to support Council unity, DRC sovereignty, civilian protection and African-led peace processes.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently voted in favour of DRC resolutions and supports the draft’s focus on sovereignty, non-interference, protection of civilians, and tracking illicit resource flows. With no requested changes and a position of support, it would vote yes and explain its support briefly.
reasons.Panama: Panama’s request on OP16 was only partially accepted, but the draft advances its core priorities on DRC sovereignty, peace and accountability and is clearly preferable to no Council action. Panama therefore supports the resolution while noting its continued preference for firmer sanctions language.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The draft aligns with the Republic of Korea’s prior support for consensus-based Council action on the DRC, its emphasis on sovereignty, civilian protection and humanitarian access, and it does not conflict with ROK interests. As an elected member, ROK would vote in favour and explain its vote to support de-escalation and regional peace efforts.
reasons.Russian Federation: The final text partially accommodates Russian concerns by avoiding explicit Rwanda-specific attribution in key paragraphs and by emphasizing verification and regional consultation, so Moscow can vote in favour while registering reservations on sanctions readiness. Supporting the French draft also preserves Council unity on a regional crisis where Russia has consistently backed African-led political processes.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone is a co-penholder with France on DRC resolutions and has consistently supported Council action upholding DRC sovereignty, civilian protection, and regional peace efforts. The draft aligns with those priorities and its last negotiation position was support with no requested changes.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia is a strong supporter of DRC sovereignty, civilian protection, international law, and UN peacekeeping mandates; the draft aligns with its prior votes and stated priorities. It would vote in favour while emphasizing accountability and safeguards for MONUSCO.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supported the draft in negotiations and has no requested changes; its foreign policy prioritizes sovereignty, non-interference, African-led peace efforts, and protection of civilians and peacekeepers. Voting yes is consistent with that record.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft aligns with the UK’s established position condemning M23 advances and external support, upholding DRC sovereignty, backing regional diplomacy, humanitarian access and MONUSCO safeguards. As a penholder-aligned permanent member, the UK would vote in favour and explain support before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supported the draft in negotiations and would not block a resolution demanding M23 withdrawal and external force withdrawal, even though it falls short of explicitly naming Rwanda. It would vote yes while publicly criticizing the omission and calling out Rwandan support to M23.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region, and we demand the immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of M23 and of all foreign military forces present without the consent of the DRC. Algeria stresses that this crisis must be resolved through African-led diplomacy, in particular the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and through full respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also stress that any consideration of targeted sanctions must be based on credible and verifiable information, with due process and in close consultation with the African Union and regional mechanisms.
before.China:
Mr. President,

China supports the draft resolution and will vote in favour. We thank France as penholder and welcome the constructive adjustments made to the text, which help the Council deliver a balanced and unified message while avoiding the singling out of any particular party. China remains firmly committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. We call on all parties to immediately cease hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, protect civilians, humanitarian personnel and peacekeepers, and facilitate safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. The priority now is to de-escalate the situation and create conditions for a political settlement through the Luanda and Nairobi processes, with Angola’s mediation and the ownership of regional organizations. China supports efforts to end all support to armed groups, based on credible and verifiable information and in full respect for the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. We encourage the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda to resume dialogue, restore mutual trust and resolve their security concerns through peaceful means. The international community should continue to support African-led solutions and provide humanitarian assistance to the affected populations. China will continue to play a constructive role in promoting peace and stability in the Great Lakes region.
before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour. The scale of suffering in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and the risk of a wider regional war require this Council to speak clearly: M23 must halt its offensive and withdraw from Goma, Bukavu and all occupied areas; external support to armed groups must end; humanitarian access must be safe and unimpeded; and MONUSCO must be able to implement its mandate. Denmark would have preferred OP16 to require the Sanctions Committee to prioritise designations, but the text’s readiness to consider targeted measures is an important step. We call on all parties to comply immediately, and on this Council to remain ready to act if they do not.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution, which we have submitted to the Council. The situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is extremely grave: the M23 offensive, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu, the humanitarian catastrophe and the risk of a wider regional war require a clear and firm response from this Council. France condemns in the strongest terms all direct and indirect support to M23, including the presence and operational support of Rwandan forces on Congolese territory, as reported by United Nations officials and the Group of Experts. This resolution demands the immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, and the withdrawal of all foreign military forces present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo without its consent. It reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. It also calls for safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and accountability for violations. France fully supports the Luanda and Nairobi processes and calls for the resumption of direct dialogue between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, implementation of the ceasefire and the Luanda commitments, and neutralization of the FDLR. This text provides a balanced and operational basis for the Council to act. France calls on all members to support it.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the escalation of violence in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, in particular the M23 offensive, the capture of Goma and Bukavu, and reports of external military support. Greece reaffirms its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas, and the immediate withdrawal of all foreign military forces operating without the consent of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We stress the obligation of all parties to protect civilians, ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and comply fully with international humanitarian law and international human rights law. Greece supports the Luanda and Nairobi processes, the mediation of Angola, and MONUSCO’s mandate, including its support to SAMIDRC consistent with resolution 2746, without MONUSCO involvement in combat operations. Accountability for atrocities and attacks against peacekeepers and humanitarian personnel must be ensured, and we urge all parties to return to dialogue and de-escalation.
before.Guyana:
Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution.

We are deeply alarmed by the escalation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu, the continuing M23 offensive, the humanitarian suffering and the risk of a wider regional war. Guyana reaffirms its firm commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and all States in the region, and to the obligation of all States to refrain from the threat or use of force and from interference in the affairs of other States.

Guyana supports the draft’s clear demands for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas, and the cessation of all direct and indirect support to armed groups, including external military support and the withdrawal of foreign forces operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo without its consent. We also welcome the text’s attention to the protection of civilians, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, accountability, the safety of MONUSCO and SAMIDRC personnel, and the centrality of the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We appreciate that our proposal concerning OP16 was taken on board, so that any consideration of targeted measures is anchored in the 1533 sanctions regime and in credible and verifiable information.

Guyana remains of the view that the Council must act with unity and in support of African-led diplomacy. We therefore vote in favour of this resolution and call on all parties to comply fully with its provisions.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the humanitarian and security situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and condemn all violence against civilians, humanitarian personnel and peacekeepers. Pakistan has consistently upheld the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region, and we call on all external actors to cease support to armed groups and to respect the principle of non-interference. We welcome the resolution’s emphasis on tracking financial flows linked to the illegal exploitation of natural resources, a key driver of conflict. We also stress that lasting peace requires inclusive political dialogue through the Luanda and Nairobi processes. Pakistan supports the resolution.
before.Panama: Panama thanks the penholder and welcomes the resolution’s clear reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region, its condemnation of M23 and of all external support to armed groups, and its strong humanitarian and protection provisions. We would have preferred the Council to signal more explicitly its intention to adopt targeted sanctions where credible and verifiable evidence warrants, but the text preserves that path and strengthens accountability. Panama will therefore vote in favour and urges all parties to cease hostilities, withdraw foreign forces operating without consent, protect civilians, facilitate humanitarian access and return to the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea votes in favour of this draft resolution. We remain gravely concerned by the escalation of violence in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, including the M23’s military advances, the catastrophic humanitarian impact, and the risk of a wider regional conflict. We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and of all States in the region, and we call for the immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of M23 from all occupied areas. We condemn all support to armed groups and stress that all foreign military forces present in the DRC without its consent must withdraw without delay. We underline the need for full respect for international humanitarian law and human rights law, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and accountability for serious violations. The Republic of Korea also supports the Luanda and Nairobi processes and MONUSCO’s mandate, including the protection of civilians, and urges renewed diplomacy to achieve a lasting political settlement.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will support this draft resolution. We share the Council’s grave concern at the deteriorating situation in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and its humanitarian consequences for civilians. We consistently advocate respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region, and we call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a lasting political settlement through the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We welcome that the final text does not make unverified attributions and stresses the need to verify reports of external military support through the relevant United Nations and regional mechanisms. At the same time, we stress that any consideration of sanctions under the 1533 Committee must be strictly based on credible and verifiable information, respect due process and the principle of non-interference, and proceed in close consultation with the African Union and regional mechanisms. The Council’s action should support regional diplomacy, not replace it. We therefore vote in favour.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone wishes to thank France for its leadership and all Council members for their constructive engagement on this urgent draft resolution. The situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached a deeply alarming point: the offensive by M23, the capture of Goma and Bukavu, the grave humanitarian consequences, and the risk of a wider regional war require the Council to speak clearly and act with unity. Sierra Leone therefore supports this resolution, which reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo; demands the immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of M23 from occupied areas; condemns all direct or indirect support to armed groups; calls for the withdrawal of foreign military forces operating without the consent of the Democratic Republic of the Congo; and stresses the protection of civilians, unimpeded humanitarian access, accountability, and the full implementation of the Luanda and Nairobi processes. We also value the resolution’s reaffirmation of MONUSCO’s mandate, including its support to SAMIDRC within existing parameters and without involvement in combat operations. Sierra Leone votes in favour.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this resolution. We remain gravely alarmed by the continued M23 offensive, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu, the catastrophic humanitarian impact, and reports of external military support to armed groups. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the unconditional withdrawal of M23 and of all foreign forces operating in the DRC without its consent, and full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC and all States in the region. We stress the imperative of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, safeguarding MONUSCO and humanitarian personnel, and ensuring accountability for serious violations. Slovenia supports the Luanda and Nairobi processes and urges the DRC and Rwanda to de-escalate, restore dialogue, and implement their commitments. We also underline that MONUSCO’s support to SAMIDRC must remain consistent with resolution 2746 (2024), applicable United Nations policies, and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and must not involve MONUSCO in combat operations.
before.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour of this resolution. We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region, and we underscore the obligation of all States to refrain from the threat or use of force and from interference in the internal affairs of others. Somalia condemns all violence and all support to armed groups, including M23, and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, unimpeded humanitarian access, and the safety of MONUSCO and humanitarian personnel. We support the Luanda and Nairobi processes and urge the DRC and Rwanda to de-escalate, restore dialogue and pursue a peaceful settlement through African-led mechanisms. Somalia believes this resolution is balanced and action-oriented, and we will continue to support regional efforts to prevent a wider war and address the humanitarian crisis.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the escalation of violence in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu by M23, the humanitarian suffering, and reports of external military support and the presence of foreign forces without the consent of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This resolution sends a clear message that all support to M23 must cease, that M23 must withdraw from occupied areas, and that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo must be respected. The United Kingdom strongly supports the Luanda and Nairobi processes and urges the parties to return to dialogue in good faith. We also stress the importance of unimpeded humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for violations, and continued support for MONUSCO’s mandate, including protection of civilians and the safeguards in resolution 2746. We call on all parties to comply fully with their obligations under international law and with this resolution.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. It sends a clear and necessary message that M23 must halt its offensive and withdraw from Goma, Bukavu and all other areas it occupies, and that all external support to armed groups must end immediately. We regret that the text still does not explicitly name the Rwandan Defence Forces, despite the extensive and credible evidence of their deployment in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and their support to M23. The Council should not resort to euphemism in the face of such facts. We call on Rwanda to end all support to M23 and withdraw its forces, and we call on all parties to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The United States will continue to support the Luanda and Nairobi processes and will press for accountability, including through targeted sanctions where credible evidence warrants.

after.France:
Mr. President,

France welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution, which we submitted to the Council. At a moment when the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing a grave escalation, including the capture of Goma and Bukavu and the risk of a wider regional war, the Council has spoken with one voice. This is essential, and we thank all members for their constructive engagement.

The message of this resolution is clear and must be implemented without delay. M23 must immediately cease hostilities and withdraw from all areas it occupies. All external support to M23 and to other armed groups must end. All foreign military forces present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo without its consent must withdraw. France reiterates its condemnation of the Rwandan military presence and operational support to M23 on Congolese territory, as documented by United Nations officials and the Group of Experts. The sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region must be respected.

France also stresses that the humanitarian catastrophe requires an immediate response. Civilians, humanitarian personnel and MONUSCO must be protected, and humanitarian access must be safe and unimpeded. Those responsible for violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law must be held accountable.

The resolution confirms the Council’s support for the Luanda and Nairobi processes and for the mediation of Angola. We call on the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda to resume dialogue in good faith, implement their commitments, including the FDLR neutralization plan and the disengagement plan, and de-escalate immediately.

France will follow the implementation of this resolution closely. The Council must remain ready to consider further measures, including targeted sanctions through the 1533 Committee, if the demands of this resolution are not respected. France remains fully mobilized, with its partners, for a lasting political settlement and for peace and security in the Great Lakes region.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We did so because the text as a whole calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and for a lasting political settlement through the Luanda and Nairobi processes, and because the final version avoids unverified attributions while stressing the need to verify reports of external military support through the relevant United Nations and regional mechanisms.

We note that some colleagues have attempted to interpret this resolution as naming a particular party. That is not our reading. The Council must base its decisions on credible and verifiable information, not on unsubstantiated accusations or external pressure.

At the same time, we reiterate our principled position: the crisis in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo cannot be resolved by military means. The sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of all States in the region must be fully respected. All parties, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, must de-escalate and return to dialogue. African-led mechanisms, in particular the Luanda and Nairobi processes, have no alternative, and the United Nations should support them rather than substitute for them.

We also stress that any consideration of sanctions under the 1533 Committee must be based on credible and verifiable information, with due process and in close consultation with the African Union and regional States. Sanctions must not become an instrument of unilateral pressure or interference in the internal affairs of sovereign States. We call for safe and unimpeded humanitarian access and for the safety and security of MONUSCO and SAMIDRC personnel.

The Russian Federation will continue to support efforts aimed at a lasting and just settlement in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Great Lakes region.
